# R299 — Pristine official batched-prefill settings and B570 synchronization gate
Date: 2026-10-12 (Asia/Tokyo)

## Decision

The pristine official v0.1.43 source at `7695859aa13afb248bdb4d36f9b2e95707db079d` has no generally safe parameter-only batched-prefill recipe for the stated B570 capability state (`HOST_USM=1`, `usm_atomic_host_allocations=false`). The batched path contains two host/device completion-marker protocols. A normal 32K prompt at `--prefill 8192` takes four chunks, so the cross-chunk PLE marker poll is reachable; routed nonresident, unpinned experts can independently reach the Stager marker poll even with PLE on one chunk. The source does not test the host-atomic aspect and does not fall back to a serialized route when it is absent. `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0` is not an official source control and would not repair either synchronization protocol.

There is a narrow, **conditional source-reachability candidate** for unmodified upstream: batch each text segment in a single chunk and ensure that every non-GPU expert that can be read by Prefill is a fully pinned host source, so no Stager job is queued. Example settings for an exact fresh 32K/64K text prompt are below. This is safe by source reasoning only if runtime receipts prove both conditions before the request; the CLI options alone do not guarantee them. The stock `--resident-experts` mode deliberately soft-falls back to a partial/pageable complement, and prefill sizing may be clamped for memory. Thus this candidate is not yet an admitted B570 run or a performance result. If either condition is not met, use the existing serial verify-window route for a bounded correctness control; it is not a batched measurement.

## Exact batched candidate and its preconditions

Hold the exact model, native quantized pack, profile, cache, build/runtime, prompt IDs, and other measured settings constant. For the known v0.1.43 baseline cache policy, use:

```text
--serve --max-context 262144 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --no-kv-grow
--expert-cache 128 --expert-cache-per-layer --expert-profile <same profile>
--pool-workers 5 --pcie-frac 0 --adapt-swaps 0
--short-read 0 --prefill 32768 --no-prefill-borrow --spec 4 --suffix-draft 0 --greedy
--resident-experts
environment: STRATA_PREFILL_FIRST=0 STRATA_PREFILL_STREAM_ALL=0 STRATA_PREFILL_ISSUER=0
            STRATA_VERIFY_STEPPED=1 STRATA_VERIFY_PIPE=0
```

Keep MTP absent; leave `STRATA_CKPT_REREAD`, batch slots, and pipeline windows off. For a 64K input, set the fixed chunk to `--prefill 65536` so each full text segment remains one Prefill chunk. The recipe preserves the production model/CPU expert work; it does not disable routing, PLE, or routed experts. `--no-prefill-borrow` makes the candidate use owned prefill buffers, but may make the large exact chunk fail its allocation admission. `STRATA_PREFILL_FIRST=0`, `STRATA_PREFILL_STREAM_ALL=0`, and `STRATA_PREFILL_ISSUER=0` keep the candidate on the first-chunk-off, routed-only, inline-issue variant; they are not synchronization fixes and are safe only together with the single-chunk/full-pinned predicates.

Do not submit a model request unless startup/effective-setting evidence proves all of the following: actual fresh text segment sizes and actual chunk size show each segment is one chunk (`T >= segment length`, with no clamp); no segment goes through `read_windows`; resident RAM mode completed the whole cache complement and reports it page-locked (not pageable, locked-only, or a partial soft fallback); and the actual source/prefill cache coverage confirms all nonresident expert blobs for the route are pinned. If full complement does not fit or cannot be pinned, the source's `--resident-experts` fallback explicitly leaves some experts on the mmap/file path; do not run the batched request under the assumption that it is safe. For 64K, failure to retain a 65,536-row chunk means the multi-chunk PLE poll can reappear, so abort rather than silently accepting the smaller chunk. Also require exact pre/post memory receipts and normal allocation admission; these large chunks have substantially higher workspace and host PLE-buffer demand than 8K.

Conditional safety proof:

- In request routing, `windows_ok(a,b)` accepts text only when `b-a <= short_read` (`generate.cpp:9838-9845`). `--short-read 0` rejects every nonempty segment from verify-window reading, making it enter the batched `read_part` path (`:10300-10315`). `--prefill` parses an explicit integer chunk; it does not itself select the route (`:1792-1798`). In prior v160 official records, `--short-read 65536` forced the entire 32,767-position conditioning segment through serial windows despite `--prefill 8` (`R286`).
- The batched PLE path queues the host-row upload and a `ple_done_seq` fill for each chunk, but its CPU poll of the other buffer is inside `if (c0 + T < n)` (`prefill.cpp:2327-2362`). When each `Prefill::run` segment fits a single chunk, that inter-chunk poll is unreachable. PLE still runs; this is not a PLE arithmetic ablation.
- The Stager marker hazard is conditional on Stager jobs. `Stager::buffer_free` host-polls a volatile `done_seq` that a device copy/fill writes (`prefill.cpp:364-365, 506-523`). In the normal streamed route, pinned resident source blobs get `job=-1`; unpinned blobs become Stager jobs (`:2513-2567`). With all non-GPU blobs pinned, `issue_until` takes direct pinned-host copies and does not call `stager->wait` or `issued_one`; in the routed-only path the pinned branch likewise skips staging (`:3814-3839`). `--resident-experts` attempts a whole resident complement but can soften to only the profile-ranked subset and fallback to files/pageable memory (`generate.cpp:1931-1939, 6330-6418`). Its option name is therefore insufficient evidence; require full coverage and page-locked effective state.
- The regular decode token-graph doorbell is a separate issue. The existing `STRATA_VERIFY_STEPPED=1` serializes verifier host/device handoffs; `STRATA_VERIFY_PIPE=0` disables optional overlap. R193 reviewed this ordinary verifier path with CPU expert service retained. This protects the decode transition but does not make either batched Prefill marker safe if its reachability conditions fail.

These are route conditions, not a source-provided capability guard. If exact route/source coverage cannot be observed before prompt submission, the conditional recipe cannot be claimed safe on the target.

## Exact stock fallback when the batched conditions fail

For the source-supported, slower text-only correctness control, use the existing serial windows path with `--serve --spec 4 --short-read 65536`, `STRATA_VERIFY_STEPPED=1 STRATA_VERIFY_PIPE=0`, MTP absent, regular CPU expert pool enabled, and batch/pipeline off. Hold `--max-context 262144 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --no-kv-grow` plus the same cache/profile/model. This routes the 32K or 64K text segment through verifier windows and bypasses Prefill's Stager and PLE marker loops. It is not the requested batched optimization and may take thousands of windows; do not compare its prompt tok/s as a batched-prefill result. Images are ineligible for the window route and require a separate qualification.

## Why common parameter tweaks do not qualify the ordinary batched route

- `--prefill 8192` on a 32,768-ID prompt batches 32,767 conditioning positions as 8192 + 8192 + 8192 + 8191, reaching the second/third PLE-buffer wait. At 64K it also remains multi-chunk. `--prefill auto` does not route the request safely; bare auto has an 8192 ceiling and remains batched once selected.
- Increasing chunk/ring size can postpone/reduce buffer reuse but does not prove the exact one-chunk route was retained or remove Stager jobs. A chunk clamp restores the PLE wait. `STRATA_STAGER_RING` only changes Stager ring depth.
- `STRATA_PLE_BATCH=0` changes PLE arithmetic selection, not its double-buffer upload lifetime/marker protocol. `STRATA_PREFILL_FIRST=0`, `STRATA_PREFILL_ISSUER=0`, `STRATA_PREFILL_STREAM_ALL=0`, copy-engine choice and `STRATA_PREFILL_SYNC=1` do not replace the PLE marker with a queue wait or make the Stager marker supported (`R238`).
- `--resident-experts` by itself is not a proof: its full-complement attempt may fail and its designed soft fallback preserves only what fits; require effective complete page-locked coverage. A routed source miss that is pageable or mapped from disk can still reach the Stager poll even with CPU share 0.
- `--no-pool`, `--no-capture`, or an all-resident GPU-only workaround is not a valid substitution for the requested full quantized model route. Keep CPU misses computed and included.
- `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE` is absent from the pristine official source tree; R193 identifies it as a Xe batched-prefill CPU/GPU split setting, not an official synchronization control. Neither host atomic absence nor a B570-capability mismatch triggers an official source rejection/fallback on the batched path.

## Source/report provenance

Pristine official worktree inspected read-only: `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/Niko1221/Strata/.worktree/bench-upstream-v0143-pristine-20261012`, pinned by the parent to revision `7695859aa13afb248bdb4d36f9b2e95707db079d`. No Git command was run. Source identities:

- `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`, SHA-256 `8112c1808dc317e89d9635ad1b6e46b080fc16e67a0b2f63923d5231f355fa07`.
- `sycl/src/prefill/prefill.cpp`, SHA-256 `110fc8bdc7d62057031c2b76317dbcfd686d6ab37f37548e311bc2fb27920d6d`.
- `sycl/src/core/verify.cpp`, SHA-256 `fa054779c47fd22abea9d9d71d55ab01af1df7d745f87e52e8ff3538a732d11e`.

Read supplied registry v171 and reports R286 (official 32K/64K setting matrix), R260 (route/host-atomic boundary), R238 (large-batched route audit), R219 (single-chunk/full-pinned candidate caveat), and R193 (safe verifier-window handoff). They establish that the prior official 32K `--prefill 8 --short-read 65536` literal run is a serial-width-8 baseline, not an optimized batched comparison. No update report/run receipt or active Main state was read.

## Limits

This is a static source/reports audit, not a B570 execution proof, memory-fit result, correctness result or performance measurement. The conditional batched candidate is not qualified until exact 32K/64K effective chunk, fully pinned complement coverage, all model allocations, output/state correctness, first decode transition, normal close and host/device fault results are captured on the pristine binary/runtime. No source edit, test/import/build, GPU, process/service operation, Git operation, cleanup or large capture was performed. No new external web source was needed; conclusions are pinned to the official upstream source at the exact revision above.
